title: Exception (Al-Istithnāʾ)
source: Original instructional lesson authored for this application (syllabus ref: Haywood & Nahmad Ch. 51; Ryding Ch. 37)
objectives: Vocalize the excepted noun (al-mustathnā) after إِلَّا across affirmative, complete-negative, and incomplete-negative clauses.
Use the exception nouns غَيْرُ and سِوَى governing the following noun in the genitive.
recallPrompt: From Chapter 28: How did إِلَّا function in لَمْ يَقُلْ إِلَّا الحَقَّ?

sections.heading: The Three Environments of إِلَّا
sections.body: The case of the noun following إِلَّا ('except / only') depends on whether the sentence is affirmative or negative, and whether the general category (al-mustathnā minhu) is mentioned.

sections.label: Case Rules for Al-Istithnāʾ
sections.summary: 1) Affirmative & complete: MUST be ACCUSATIVE (حَضَرَ الطُّلَّابُ إِلَّا وَاحِدًا). 2) Negative & complete: either accusative OR badal matching the category. 3) Negative & incomplete (mustathnā minhu omitted): إِلَّا is grammatically transparent ('only'), and the noun takes whatever case the verb requires (مَا قَرَأْتُ إِلَّا كِتَابًا). 4) غَيْرُ / سِوَى take the case that would have fallen after إِلَّا and govern the following noun in the GENITIVE.

sections.translation: I spoke nothing but the truth.
sections.irab: مَا: نَافِيَةٌ | قُلْتُ: فِعْلٌ وَفَاعِلٌ | إِلَّا: أَدَاةُ حَصْرٍ | الصِّدْقَ: مَفْعُولٌ بِهِ مَنْصُوبٌ
sections.notes: Because the general category is omitted in a negative clause, إِلَّا acts as a restrictive particle ('only') and الصِّدْقَ is simply the direct object of قُلْتُ.

sections.heading: Quick Test for Incomplete Negative
sections.body: Mentally cover مَا and إِلَّا: if the remaining words form a complete sentence (قُلْتُ الصِّدْقَ), assign the normal case!
